```json
{
  "subtype": "faceted_decomposition",
  "concept": "praise_and_complaint_drivers",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "praise_word_count",
      "is_constitutive_facet": false,
      "role": "restatement",
      "rationale": "A bare count of praise words is a mechanical proxy for the presence of praise itself, not a distinct constitutive aspect of what DRIVES praise. It restates the sentiment magnitude rather than naming a driver (e.g., product quality, price, delivery)."
    },
    {
      "name": "complaint_word_count",
      "is_constitutive_facet": false,
      "role": "restatement",
      "rationale": "Symmetric to praise_word_count: a count of complaint words measures the complaint signal, not an aspect/facet of the underlying drivers. It also overlaps heavily with praise_word_count as a generic polarity-count pair."
    },
    {
      "name": "review_detail_level",
      "is_constitutive_facet": false,
      "role": "external_predictor",
      "rationale": "How detailed a review is may correlate with review informativeness but is not a part-of the drivers of praise/complaint; it is a property of the review text, an external predictor at best."
    },
    {
      "name": "emotional_intensity",
      "is_constitutive_facet": false,
      "role": "restatement",
      "rationale": "Generic sentiment/emotion intensity is a bare affect measure. It captures how strongly the reviewer feels, not WHAT drives that feeling, so it restates polarity strength rather than decomposing the drivers."
    },
    {
      "name": "aspects_discussed",
      "is_constitutive_facet": false,
      "role": "external_predictor",
      "rationale": "A single count of aspects discussed points toward the right idea (drivers are product/service aspects) but does not itself enumerate any facet; it is a meta-count, not a named constitutive aspect such as quality, price, shipping, or usability."
    }
  ],
  "facet_columns": [],
  "non_facet_columns": [
    "praise_word_count",
    "complaint_word_count",
    "review_detail_level",
    "emotional_intensity",
    "aspects_discussed"
  ],
  "mutual_exclusivity": 0.3,
  "exhaustiveness": 0.05,
  "rationale": "The concept 'praise_and_complaint_drivers' should decompose into constitutive aspects that people praise or complain about -- e.g., product quality, price/value, shipping/delivery, customer service, usability, durability. None of the added columns name such facets. Instead they are mechanical magnitude measures (praise/complaint word counts, emotional intensity), text-property proxies (detail level), or a bare aspect count. praise_word_count and complaint_word_count are near-mirror generic polarity counts that overlap in what they capture, and emotional_intensity again reflects polarity magnitude, lowering mutual exclusivity. Since no genuine driver facet is present, exhaustiveness against the concept is near zero. The set fails the meronymy test."
}
```
